diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: The induction attempts to bound every $k$-column submatrix, but a false X3C instance can contain two disjoint sets. Their columns are orthonormal and have volume $1$, exceeding the claimed base bound $2\sqrt{2}/3$. The overlap is guaranteed only for a full $M$-column selection, not for arbitrary subcollections.

failure_location.quote: For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or in two elements.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the induction by a direct argument: in a false instance any $M$-column set contains an overlapping pair; adding columns cannot increase volume, so its volume is at most that of the overlapping pair, which is at most $2\sqrt{2}/3$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem t_vol is invalid, so the derived no-PTAS result and its dependent Theorem t_sopt are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Invalid induction base in volume no-PTAS proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement remains true and the proof can be repaired by a short local argument using the guaranteed overlapping pair and monotonicity of volume.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: A false X3C instance can have two disjoint sets. Their two-column submatrix has largest singular value $1$, which is below the claimed lower bound $2/\sqrt{3}$. The overlap is only guaranteed for the full $M$-column selection, so the induction hypothesis is false for smaller subcollections.

failure_location.quote:
For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or
in two elements.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the guaranteed overlapping pair in the full $M$-column set and singular value interlacing to obtain $\|\mc\|_2\ge \|\hat\mc_2\|_2\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem t_2m is invalid, so the derived no-PTAS result and its dependent Theorem t_sr are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Invalid induction base in two-norm no-PTAS proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement remains true and the proof can be repaired by a short local argument using the guaranteed overlapping pair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: A false X3C instance can have two disjoint sets. Their two-column submatrix has smallest singular value $1$, so the pseudo-inverse two-norm is $1$, below the claimed lower bound $\sqrt{3/2}$. The overlap is only guaranteed for the full $M$-column selection.

failure_location.quote:
For $k=2$, two distinct sets can overlap in one or
in two elements.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the guaranteed overlapping pair and singular value interlacing to obtain $\|\mc^\dagger\|_2\ge 1/\sigma_2(\hat\mc_2)\ge\sqrt{3/2}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem t_ssv is invalid, so the derived no-PTAS result and its dependent Theorem t_cd are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Invalid induction base in pseudo-inverse two-norm no-PTAS proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement remains true and the proof can be repaired by a short local argument using the guaranteed overlapping pair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then any collection $\mathcal{K}$ of cardinality $k=M$ has at least two sets $\mathcal{K}_i$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ with $i\neq j$ and a non-empty intersection.

issues.failure_explanation: In a false X3C instance, a selected $M$-column set must contain at least one overlapping pair, but it can also contain many disjoint columns. The assumption that any two columns overlap is false and is used to make the induction hypothesis apply to submatrices.

failure_location.quote: Assume that X3C instance is false, and assume that any two columns of~$\mc$ overlap.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false assumption and apply Lemma l_fi to separate the guaranteed overlapping pair from the remaining $k-2$ columns, obtaining $\|\mc^\dagger\|_F^2\ge \|\hat\mc_2^\dagger\|_F^2+(k-2)\ge k+1/4$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem t_pi is invalid, so its dependent Theorems t_pi3 and t_fcond are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Unjustified assumption that every pair of columns overlaps
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement remains true and the proof can be repaired by a short local argument using the guaranteed overlapping pair and Lemma l_fi.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, all singular values of $\mc$ are equal to~1, and $\mc$ has orthonormal columns.

issues.failure_explanation: The equality $\rvol(\mc)=1$ only forces all singular values of $\mc$ to be equal; it does not force them to equal $1$. For example, $\mc=2I_2$ has $\rvol(\mc)=1$ but its columns have norm $2$ and are not orthonormal. The unit-norm hypothesis is missing.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\rvol(\mc) = 1$  if and only if the columns of $\mc$ are orthonormal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the columns of $\mc$ have unit norm, or change the conclusion to say that all singular values are equal, equivalently that $\mc$ is a scalar multiple of a matrix with orthonormal columns.
issues.overall_effect: The general equality characterization in Lemma lem:orth-2 is false. Its use in the unit-norm reduction is not invalidated, but the stated lemma is incorrect.
issues.title: Relative volume equality does not imply orthonormal columns without unit-norm assumption
issues.why_classification: The false statement is repaired by a short local condition or conclusion change, and the paper's main unit-norm applications survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Since $\sigma_1(\mc)\ge 1$, the quantity $(k/\sigma_1(\mc)^p)^{1/p}$ is at most $k^{1/p}$, not at least $k^{1/p}$. The displayed chain therefore does not prove the claimed lower bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the faulty chain with a valid proof of $\|\mc^\dagger\|_{(p)}\ge k^{1/p}$, for example by convexity of $x^{-p/2}$ together with $\sum_j \sigma_j(\mc)^2=k$, or by AM-GM using $\vol(\mc)\le 1$.
issues.overall_effect: The Schatten $p$-norm bullet of Lemma l_pinv is not proved as written, so the Schatten $p$-norm part of Theorem t_pi7 is unsupported.
issues.title: Reversed inequality in Schatten p-norm pseudo-inverse proof
issues.why_classification: The lemma statement is true and the proof can be repaired by a standard local argument, preserving all claims.

issues.failure_explanation: For $p>2$ the claimed squared inequality is false. Taking $\mc=I_2$, $\mc_1=e_1$, $\mc_2=e_2$, and $p=4$ gives the left side $\|I_2\|_4^2=\sqrt{2}$ but the right side $1+1=2$. The proof incorrectly treats the Schatten $q$-norm of a block diagonal matrix as the sum of the $q$-norms of its blocks.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the squared inequality by the correct $p$-th power inequality $\|\mc^\dagger\|_{(p)}^p\ge \|\mc_1^\dagger\|_{(p)}^p+\|\mc_2^\dagger\|_{(p)}^p$, or state the correct block-diagonal norm formula.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma l_pi1 is false as stated, so the advertised squared Schatten $p$-norm lower bound for partitioned pseudo-inverses is invalid.
issues.title: False squared Schatten p-norm partition inequality
issues.why_classification: The result is false and its repair weakens the inequality from a squared to a $p$-th power bound; the correction is local but not merely cosmetic.
